title: Financial Statements
description: Income statement, balance sheet and statement of cash flows.
html:
The major financial statements

Financial statements organize accounting information into reports that help users understand a company's financial performance and financial position.

Income Statement

Reports revenues and expenses over a period of time.

Revenue − Expenses = Net Income

Balance Sheet

Reports assets, liabilities and equity at a specific date.

Assets = Liabilities + Equity

Statement of Cash Flows

Explains changes in cash during a period.

Operating · Investing · Financing

Statement of Equity

Explains changes in owners' or shareholders' equity during a period.

Income Statement Example

Service Revenue $50,000
Salary Expense ($20,000)
Rent Expense ($8,000)
Utilities Expense ($2,000)
Net Income $20,000

Balance Sheet Example

Total Assets $100,000
Total Liabilities $40,000
Total Equity $60,000
Liabilities + Equity $100,000

Statement of Cash Flows

Three categories

  • Operating: cash flows related primarily to normal business operations.
  • Investing: cash flows involving certain long-term assets and investments.
  • Financing: cash flows involving debt and owners/shareholders.

Connecting the statements

The financial statements are not isolated reports. Information from the accounting system flows between them.

As you move into intermediate and CPA-level accounting, understanding these connections becomes increasingly important.

Fundamentals complete

You now have the foundation needed to begin studying accounting in much greater depth.

The next stage will build on these concepts with more difficult transactions, calculations, rules, and financial reporting topics.

quiz.prompt: Which financial statement reports assets, liabilities and equity at a specific date?
quiz.explanation: The balance sheet reports a company's assets, liabilities and equity at a specific point in time.
